solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mostly light brown dust in the air?

indicators.note: mostly says the colour word loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: hazel is a light greenish-brown colour, as of hazelnuts

explanation.surface: Someone describes airborne dust as being mostly light brown in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A haze is a thin mist of fine particles such as dust or smoke hanging in the air.

clue.text: Superb exterior to masculine perfection

indicators.note: exterior to says the first word sits outside the next piece, wrapping round it

parts.note: ace means superb, first-rate
M is the standard abbreviation for masculine in grammar

explanation.surface: A grooming advert praising a superb exterior that brings out masculine perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement, the summit of excellence.

clue.text: Whisky misuse is reduced by half

indicators.note: reduced by half says only the front half of the synonym for misuse is kept

parts.note: to maltreat is to misuse or treat badly

explanation.surface: A temperance message: whisky misuse has been cut by fifty per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: The word to halve is MALTREAT, a synonym the clue never prints; its first four letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is short for malt whisky, a spirit distilled from malted barley.

clue.text: Live in impressive tower

indicators.note: in says the word for live goes inside the word for impressive

parts.note: mint means in perfect condition, hence impressive
are means exist or live, as in 'we are'

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch: come and live in an impressive tower block.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Investigator's regret about supporting special relationship

definitions.note: read as 'Investigator is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the reversed piece underneath the first

parts.note: rapport is a close, harmonious relationship

indicators.note: about says the word for regret is turned round

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An investigator voices regret about backing the US-UK 'special relationship'.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Investigator's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapporteur is someone appointed to investigate and report, such as a UN special rapporteur.

clue.text: Sickly, uneasy state, getting off ship with bag in front

indicators.note: in front puts the bag word before the rest

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in an animal or plant

indicators.note: getting off, as passengers disembark, says the ship letters leave the word

parts.note: chariness is wariness, an uneasy state of caution
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A seasick passenger in an uneasy state disembarks clutching a bag held in front.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARINESS loses its final SS, leaving CHARINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine means excessively sweet or sentimental, so cloying, sickly.

clue.text: Boarding national airline, bully missing first of ballots

indicators.note: boarding, getting on a plane, says the next piece goes inside the airline

parts.note: El Al is Israel's national airline

indicators.note: missing first says the word for bully loses its opening letter

parts.note: to hector is to bully

explanation.surface: A passenger boarding the national airline turns bully, but misses the first of the ballots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' reads as getting on a plane, but here it means sitting inside the airline's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral describes things relating to elections and voting, so to ballots.

clue.text: Waterfowl heading away from dam site

indicators.note: heading away says the opening letter of the place is removed

parts.note: Aswan in Egypt is the site of the Aswan High Dam on the Nile

explanation.surface: Birds flying away from the site of a dam on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a large long-necked bird living on lakes and rivers.

clue.text: Put new mortar in after salvo evacuated offensive detail?

indicators.note: after puts the mortar word behind the emptied salvo
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of salvo remain

parts.note: to repoint brickwork is to put new mortar in its joints

explanation.surface: Builders repair masonry after a military salvo empties the fort, a detail of the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive detail?' is cryptic: an aspect of a matter that gives offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore point is a subject that upsets someone, a touchy issue that gives offence.

clue.text: Turn out flat, stretched over back of frame

parts.note: even means flat, level

indicators.note: over says the word for stretched is turned back to front

parts.note: taut means stretched tight

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of frame

explanation.surface: Canvas laid flat and stretched over the back of a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to happen as a result, to come to pass, which is to turn out.

clue.text: Head teachers' brotherhood

definitions.meaning: the National Union of Teachers, a British teachers' trade union, a brotherhood of members

explanation.surface: A head teacher's fellowship of colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the skull, and the National Union of Teachers was a UK union.

clue.text: Humming part of hornpipe pirates recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pirates dancing a hornpipe, recalled while humming part of the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Humming part' as the definition, but 'part of' signals the hidden letters, leaving 'Humming' (smelly) alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for smelling strongly, and ripe likewise means pungent.

clue.text: Nod and wait in order to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word for waiting in order is spoken

parts.note: to queue is to wait in line in turn

explanation.surface: Someone nods and waits in line so as to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod can be a signal to act, just as a prompt to an actor is.

clue.text: Inventor of global disc part housing wheel-locking mechanism

indicators.note: housing says the abbreviation contains the mechanism

parts.note: a ratchet is a toothed wheel with a catch letting it turn one way only

explanation.surface: A technical description of a disc component that houses a wheel lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'global disc' is the Discworld, a flat world-disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Pratchett created Discworld, a flat planet carried on the backs of elephants and a turtle.

clue.text: Sensible Victorian remained upright, repressing temptation's commonest aspect

parts.note: a prude, someone with strait-laced Victorian values

indicators.note: repressing says the reversed word holds the next letter down inside it
in a down clue, upright says the word for remained reads from the bottom up

parts.note: lain, as in 'had lain idle', means remained
T occurs three times in temptation, more than any other letter

explanation.surface: A sensible Victorian stayed upright, suppressing the commonest form of temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIN reads upward as NIAL, and T goes inside to make NTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudential means showing prudence, careful and wise, so sensible.

clue.text: Whatever involves verse's still put in book like this?

indicators.note: involves says the word for whatever wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: any means whatever, as in 'any book'
tho' is a poetic form of 'though', meaning still or yet
to log is to enter or put in a record book

explanation.surface: Whatever contains verse is still put into a book like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: 'book' serves in both readings. THOLOG goes between the N and Y of ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a book collecting poems or other writings.

clue.text: Coupled prisoner and prison were worrying

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
jug is slang for prison
ate, as in 'what ate you', means were worrying

explanation.surface: Two linked inmates, a prisoner and his prison, were fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugate means joined together in pairs, especially in chemistry or biology.

clue.text: Having left for a run, run smoothly, getting a stitch

indicators.note: having one thing in place of another says a letter is swapped in
for, as in exchanging one for another, marks the letter being replaced

parts.note: an engine purrs when it runs smoothly
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A runner turned left, ran smoothly, and then got a stitch.
explanation.walkthrough: One R of PURR becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Purl is a knitting stitch, the reverse of plain or knit stitch.

clue.text: Sarcastic dig?

definitions.meaning: an excavation dug for a road or railway

explanation.surface: A sarcastic jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is hurtful; a railway cutting is a trench dug through high ground.

clue.text: Given guidance, that is way to spin top

indicators.note: to spin, turn round, says the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: led means given guidance
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Instructions on the way to spin a top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreidel is a four-sided spinning top played with at Hanukkah.

clue.text: Avoid holding hostage, regularly involving duress

indicators.note: holding says the word for avoid contains the letters that follow

parts.note: to shun is to avoid

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of hostage

explanation.surface: Advice in a kidnapping: avoid holding a hostage, which involves duress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun wedding or deal is one made under pressure, as if at gunpoint.

clue.text: Small bricks drop, dumping tons

indicators.note: dumping says the letter for tons is removed

parts.note: to let go is to drop

explanation.surface: A builder drops small bricks, dumping them by the ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is a brand of small interlocking plastic toy bricks.

clue.text: Perhaps overstuff overcoat, having eaten noodle soup

indicators.note: having eaten says the coat word takes the soup inside it

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat
pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Someone overstuffs their overcoat after eating noodle soup.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to pad and cover furniture; overstuffing a chair is one example.

clue.text: Move over, easily demolishing lead of marathon runner

indicators.note: demolishing says the first letter of marathon is knocked out

parts.note: to skim is to glide lightly over a surface

indicators.note: lead of picks the first letter of marathon

explanation.surface: A marathon runner moves over, easily demolishing the race leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like part of the marathon scene; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, like those under a sledge, sliding over snow.

clue.text: Wrap up one of many sentences?

definitions.meaning: to ... pipes is to wrap them in insulation
a habitual convict who has served many prison terms

explanation.surface: A writer wraps up one of many sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging insulates pipes; an old lag is a repeat prisoner with many terms served.

clue.text: Man behind losing jacket

indicators.note: losing jacket says the outer letters, the covering, are stripped off

parts.note: a bottom is a behind, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A man trailing behind after losing his jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's first name, such as Otto von Bismarck.

clue.text: Possible confirmation of leader for Camelot, not united in joint complaint

indicators.note: not says the letter for united is left out

parts.words: Possible confirmation of leader for Camelot
parts.note: asked who leads Camelot, one might confirm 'Arthur it is'
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A Camelot leader's disunity among knights is a joint complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase ARTHUR IT IS drops its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is painful inflammation of the joints, a disease affecting them.

clue.text: Cover head, somewhat ostrich-like American cousin

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to cover one's head, like an ostrich hiding, said of an American cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: See Yorkshireman's rug?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
rug is slang for a wig, a hairpiece

explanation.surface: Look at a Yorkshireman's rug.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yorkshireman says 't' wig' for 'the wig'.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British for to understand, as in 'I see'.

clue.text: With energy fully extracted, piped waste spoils

indicators.note: with joins energy to the removal signal that follows
fully extracted says every instance of the energy letter comes out

parts.note: sewage is waste carried away in pipes
E is the physics symbol for energy, here taken out twice

explanation.surface: Waste is piped away once all useful energy has been extracted from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods or loot, the spoils of a theft.

clue.text: Caprice hasn't the heart for change

indicators.note: hasn't the heart says the middle letters are taken out

parts.note: a vagary is a whim or caprice

explanation.surface: A capricious person lacks the heart to make a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or make different, so to change.

clue.text: European combined with Northern Ireland in backing thread promoting unity

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, combined with, as in 'study-cum-bedroom'

indicators.note: in puts the province's letters inside the reversed thread
backing says the thread word is read backwards

parts.note: lace is a thread or cord, as in a shoelace

explanation.surface: A European joined Northern Ireland in supporting a thread of unity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in backing thread' puts NI inside ECAL, the thread word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical describes efforts to bring the Christian churches together into one.
